entries.title: Stickney mayor, board oppose data center at Hawthorne horse racing site
entries.summary: <p>Stickney officials say they oppose <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/2026/07/27/hawthorne-race-course-horse-track-buyer-data-center-developer-stickney-cicero-ai-artificial-intelligence" >construction of a data center</a> at the site of the now-closed Hawthorne Race Course, which closed down last month after 135 years of horse racing.</p><p>On Thursday, the village’s board of trustees voted unanimously to block any data center proposals. The moratorium states the village won’t accept changes of zoning or any approvals that would allow a data center.</p><p>“If a data center project for Hawthorne Race Course lands before the board of trustees, I will vote no,” Mayor Mitch Milenkovic, said in a statement. He cited the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/environment/2025/08/20/data-centers-ai-artificial-intelligence-chicago-illinois-great-lakes-michigan-drinking-water-jb-pritzker" >enormous demand for water</a> and <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/consumer-affairs/2026/05/13/comed-electric-customer-bills-rising-ai-data-centers-pjm-energy-costs" >power at the plants</a> and concerns about noise and other nuisances.</p><p>Stickney isn’t alone in opposing the large-scale computing centers, which are popping up across the country to support artificial intelligence applications. Mayor Brandon Johnson has asked the City Council to <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/city-hall/2026/08/11/mayor-brandon-johnson-chicago-moratorium-data-centers-new-regulations" >pass a moratorium</a> on such facilities.</p><p>Hawthorne, the oldest horse racing venue in Illinois, is being acquired after filing for bankruptcy protection.</p><p>A buyer known only as Allimac 2023 LLC agreed to pay $90 million for the property at 3501 S. Laramie Ave. in Stickney, which borders Cicero. The owner has not publicly identified itself or said what it will do with the land.</p><p>Data center developer Digital Realty is the company behind Allimac, according to commercial real estate publication The Real Deal. The publication cited multiple people familiar with the transaction.</p><p>Digital Realty developed nine Chicago-area data centers, mostly around O’Hare Airport, according to the company’s website.</p><p>Representatives of Digital Realty didn’t immediately respond to requests for comment.</p><p>Rumors of a data center replacing Hawthorne, which sits on more than 100 acres near the Cicero town line, popped up late last month. Cicero trustees passed a resolution opposing any such development in neighboring Stickney.</p><p>“The noise from the round-the-clock operation of cooling systems, backup generators, and industrial-scale equipment would diminish the quality of life for Stickney residents and the residential areas of Cicero that surround the Hawthorne site,” Milenkovic said.</p><p>The last races at Hawthorne were July 19. The racetrack’s owner filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in February.</p><p>The sale is expected to close Sept. 1.</p>
entries.author: Brett Chase

entries.title: Woman, 64, killed by stray bullet; man shot 41 times in Garfield Park murders
entries.summary: <p>Police continue to seek the assailants who chased down and shot a man 41 times, with one of the bullets mortally wounding a woman walking across the street in a double murder late Wednesday morning in the Garfield Park neighborhood.. </p><p>The 25-year-old man, who hasn't yet been identified, parked his car in the 200 block of South Pulaski Road around 11:55 a.m. Wednesday when a a black SUV parked in front of him about a minute later and two gunmen exited and opened fire toward the man, according to police reports obtained by the Sun-Times. </p><p>The man then left his car and ran north on Pulaski Road through traffic when he fell at the crosswalk about a block away, police said. </p><p>The gunmen caught up and stood over him as they continuously shot him, according to the police report. In total, he was shot 41 times in the chest and back, officials said. </p><p>The shooters then returned to their SUV and fled south before stopping nearby in the 4100 block of West Jackson Boulevard and firing more rounds, the report states. </p><p>A 64-year-old woman identified by family members as Joanne Perry was crossing the street at South Pulaski Road and West Jackson Boulevard when she was struck in the chest by gunfire, officials said. </p><p>Both the man and Perry were taken to Mount Sinai Hospital where they were pronounced dead, police said. </p><p>Relatives told <a class="Link" href="https://abc7chicago.com/post/chicago-shooting-kills-man-woman-pulaski-east-garfield-park-cpd/19703734/" target="_blank" >ABC7</a> Perry, a mother of six who was also a cancer survivor, was on her way to a nearby store when she was shot. </p><p>Shortly after the shooting, a woman lay on the ground in grief as police and bystanders gathered around her, moments after learning that Perry had been killed.</p><p>“They shot my momma,” the woman repeatedly said as residents and police officers tried to guide her from the street.</p><p>At least 40 fired shell casings were found in the 200 block of South Pulaski Road with an additional 21 casings found in the 4100 block of West Jackson Boulevard, police said. The man was believed to be the intended target. </p><p>The black SUV used by the shooters was recovered in a south alley in the 5400 block of West Harrison Street after it had been set on fire, police said. It was previously reported stolen. </p><p>No arrests have been reported. </p><p>Area 4 detectives are investigating. <br></p>

entries.title: Condenan a más de un año de prisión a exdirector de secundaria por esquema de fraude que duró casi una década
entries.summary: <p>Un exdirector de las Escuelas Públicas de Chicago (CPS) ha sido condenado a poco más de un año de prisión federal por fraude electrónico en un plan de casi una década para defraudar a varias redes escolares y organizaciones sin fines de lucro por más de $1 millón.</p><p>La jueza de distrito Lindsay C. Jenkins sentenció a Brian Metcalf, exjefe de la red de CPS y exdirector de la escuela secundaria Gage Park y de la primaria Field, a un año y un día de prisión federal el miércoles, según la Oficina del Fiscal para el Distrito Norte de Illinois.</p><p>La exproveedora de CPS, Kimberly Maddox, fue sentenciada el mes pasado a dos años de prisión y el consultor, James Campbell, quien también participó en el plan después de que este comenzara en Indiana, también fue condenado a un año y un día.</p><div class="RichTextSidebarModule Enhancement" data-module data-align-center><a class="AnchorLink" id="module-500000" name="module-500000"></a> <div class="RichTextModule-items RichTextBody"><h3>La Voz Chicago WhatsApp</h3>Encuentra más noticias en nuestro canal de WhatsApp. <a class="Link" href="https://www.whatsapp.com/channel/0029Vb0XT1XCHDylm3rCs40P" target="_blank" ><b>Síguenos.</b></a></div> </div><p>Todos están obligados a pagar $1,099,200 en concepto de restitución a las diversas instituciones que defraudaron. A principios de este año un informe del inspector general de CPS <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/education/2026/01/07/cps-watchdog-report-onlyfans-waste-fraud-investigation-education-false-grant" target="_blank" >reveló más sobre los planes de fraude del trío</a>.</p><p>De 2012 a 2017, Metcalf trabajó con la exproveedora de CPS, Kimberly Maddox, para generar facturas falsas por bienes y servicios —como capacitación en redacción de subvenciones y asesoría sobre ayuda financiera estudiantil— que nunca se prestaron. Repartieron las ganancias después de recibir el pago del distrito, dijo la oficina.</p><p>Metcalf y Maddox admitieron posteriormente el plan como parte de un acuerdo de culpabilidad en un caso federal en su contra que implicaba una trama similar para defraudar a una red de escuelas chárter en Indiana, tras salir él de CPS en 2018.</p><p>En 2025, Metcalf y Maddox admitieron que usaron la misma estrategia de facturas falsas en Tindley Accelerated Schools en Indiana, donde Metcalf fue director ejecutivo de 2019 a 2022. El esquema les dejó casi $1 millón antes de que confesaran haber hecho lo mismo en CPS, lo cual generó $88,500.</p><p>“No se tolerará a los administradores que usan su puesto para enriquecerse y privar a las familias de CPS de recursos fundamentales, ni a los proveedores que roban a CPS”, dijo el inspector general Philip Wagenknecht en un comunicado el jueves.</p><p><i>Traducido con una herramienta de inteligencia artificial (IA) y editado por los seres humanos de </i><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/la-voz" target="_blank" ><i>La Voz Chicago</i></a></p>

entries.title: Cuatro bomberos heridos, tres de ellos de gravedad, tras combatir incendio en Back of the Yards
entries.summary: <p>Un incendio en el vecindario Back of the Yards que se desató la mañana del jueves en una casa desocupada dejó cuatro bomberos heridos, tres de ellos de gravedad.</p><p>El edificio residencial comenzó a arder a eso de las 11:30 a.m. en el segundo piso de un inmueble de madera de dos unidades, en la cuadra 5400 al sur de Justine Street, según un portavoz del Departamento de Bomberos de Chicago.</p><p>Mientras combatían el fuego, cuatro bomberos resultaron heridos, tres de ellos de gravedad, según el portavoz. El cuarto fue atendido en un hospital y se encontraba en buen estado.</p><div class="RichTextSidebarModule Enhancement" data-module data-align-center><a class="AnchorLink" id="module-980000" name="module-980000"></a> <div class="RichTextModule-items RichTextBody"><h3>La Voz Chicago WhatsApp</h3>Encuentra más noticias en nuestro canal de WhatsApp. <a class="Link" href="https://www.whatsapp.com/channel/0029Vb0XT1XCHDylm3rCs40P" target="_blank" ><b>Síguenos.</b></a></div> </div><p>El edificio no fue demolido y aunque el fuego no se propagó a edificios vecinos, se extendió al ático.</p><p>La causa del incendio continúa bajo investigación.</p><p><i>Traducido con una herramienta de inteligencia artificial (IA) y editado por los seres humanos de </i><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/la-voz" target="_blank" ><i>La Voz Chicago</i></a><br></p>

entries.title: Chicago murals: Humboldt Park painting celebrates stories of faith at New Life
entries.summary: <p>Diamond V. Galindo grew up in Humboldt Park’s New Life Community Church. She stopped by after school for homework help. She spent her summers there, signing up for its programs for kids.</p><p>Artist <a class="Link" href="https://www.instagram.com/aleckscruz/" target="_blank" >Alecks Cruz</a> didn’t know any of that when he asked Galindo, whose artist name is <a class="Link" href="https://www.instagram.com/diamond_doodle_/" target="_blank" >Diamond Doodle</a>, to be lead artist for a new mural on the side of the church at 1410 N. Springfield Ave. as part of his program, <a class="Link" href="https://www.instagram.com/theheartprojectchi/" target="_blank" >The Heart Project</a>. But for Galindo, who now lives in West Ridge, it was her chance to thank the church and community that helped her as a neighborhood kid in <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/humboldt-park" >Humboldt Park</a>.</p><p>“I feel like this is my thank you note to it,” Galindo says. “When he told me they’re going to do a mural over there, I said, ‘Let’s do this.’ We did this whole mural representing the community, bringing hope and light. class="Link" href="https://newlifecenters.org/en/" target="_blank" >New Life Center</a>’s five Chicago locations. Cruz says they seek to bring healing and empowerment to kids and the community through art. This mural was done through a grant from the <a class="Link" href="https://www.richinfaith.org" target="_blank" >Rich in Faith</a> project, through which five Chicago urban ministries are collecting stories of faith in the community and using them to inspire murals, among other projects.</p><p>Participants in Rich in Faith projects don’t need to belong to a church. They just need to share how they experience God and how faith looks for them, Cruz says. For the New Life mural, the project collected stories from alumni of the church’s programs. Those programs include homework help, sports programs, jewelry making, a food pantry and more.</p><p>“Over and over, we kept hearing, ‘The church was a place where the doors were always welcome. It felt like family. There were mentors that loved me better than some of my own family members at home,’” Cruz says.</p><p>Cruz reached out to Galindo and asked if she could compile the stories and turn them into a mural with help from kids signed up for summer programs this year. Cruz likes to promote young artists and thought Galindo, a graduate of the School of the Art Institute of Chicago with Humboldt Park roots, would be perfect.</p><p>“I just knew that she was an artist,” he says. He quickly realized the project was more than just a mural to Galindo.</p><p>The resulting artwork is made up largely of pinks, greens and blues with yellow accents. The vines and flowers symbolize the church’s outreach and how its programs help kids grow while keeping them connected. The basketball represents New Life’s sports programs, and the book represents its focus on education and helping students with their homework. Humboldt Park three-flats are staggered up one side of the mural, and a mentor and student seem to be sitting on a bench nearby, reading.</p><p>Stairs lead up into the heart of a woman with blue hair, arms outstretched above the mural, with the words “beloved community” written in bubble letters over it all.</p><p>In the bottom left, a bubbly girl with pink hair — Galindo’s trademark character — is eating a Batman paleta.</p><p>“I had been craving a paleta so badly,” Galindo says about painting that section of the mural. “What I do miss about the neighborhood, I like to go out and get my ice cream. This is summer. This is my time.”</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-fullBleed> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a class="AnchorLink" id="image-a00000" name="image-a00000"></a> entries.title: Thousands in Northwest Indiana still don't have power after storms. Here's what to know.
entries.summary: <p>Northwest Indiana residents continue suffering after back-to-back storms devastated the state last week. </p><p>Near-100 mph winds and torrential downpours knocked down trees into people's homes and driveways and flooded basements and roads. Seven people died across Indiana. The storms caused widespread power outages that impacted many parts of the state. </p><p>While power has been restored for over 300,000 Hoosiers, many residents are still without power. Gary, one of Indiana's hardest hit cities, has the most customers in the state waiting for power to return, according to the state’s utility company NIPSCO.</p><p>Here's everything you need to know about what happened in Northwest Indiana and the relief efforts underway to help impacted residents. </p><h3>When will Northwest Indiana cities get their power back? </h3><p>NIPSCO reported that over 60% of its customers — roughly 370,000 — lost power during the Aug. 11 storm and subsequent days of severe weather. As of Friday morning, 331,100 customers had their lights back on, <a class="Link" href="https://www.nipsco.com/outages/power-outages" target="_blank" >according to NIPSCO</a>. </p><p>Power should be fully restored to Merrillville and East Chicago by Thursday night. Power is expected to return in Hammond by Saturday and in Munster by Monday. Gary and Portage have to wait till Tuesday for their power to turn on — two weeks after the Aug. 11 storm. <a class="Link" href="https://www.nipsco.com/outages/power-outages" target="_blank" >Here’s the full list</a> of towns still waiting on power.</p><h3>Why is it taking so long? </h3><p>As of Friday morning, 331,100 NIPSCO customers who had lost power their service restore. But in Gary, 56% of the city is still in the dark.</p><p>Part of why it’s taking longer to restore power is the city suffered the most “extensive and complex damage” from the storm, mainly because of the 99 mph winds that tore through Northwest Indiana and knocked down several large trees, a NIPSCO executive told reporters Wednesday.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Figure-content"><figcaption class="Figure-caption"><p>Krimberly Guajardo stands among tree branches on her property on the 3600 block Burr St. in Gary, Indiana, Monday, Aug. 17, 2026.</p></figcaption><span class="line"></span><div class="Figure-credit"><p>Anthony Vazquez/Sun-Times</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p>On Monday, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/weather/2026/08/17/gary-indiana-residents-without-power-deadly-storms" target="_blank" >residents showed the Sun-Times</a> the extent of the storm damage. The worst of it was caused by mature large trees crashing down onto their property. </p><p>Crews of linemen are repairing downed power lines and rebuilding destroyed electrical systems. That includes 335 damaged poles that need to be repaired or replaced and 27 outages at substations that need to be fixed before power can be restored. </p><h3>Why did ComEd restore power faster for the south suburbs?</h3><p>The same storm system that wrecked Indiana also <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/weather/2026/07/30/seven-7-confirmed-tornadoes-weather-service-illinois-monday-storms" target="_blank" >caused seven tornadoes</a> in Chicago's south suburbs. Soon after the storm, ComEd was able to restore power for the vast majority of its customers.</p><p>Melody Birmingham, the group utilities president at NiSource, NIPSCO’s parent company, explained to reporters Wednesday why it's taken the utility longer to restore power compared to ComEd. ComEd has four million customers, compared to NIPSCO's 500,000. That means the utility has a much larger staff and is better equipped to respond to outages faster.</p><h3>Are schools still closed? </h3><p>The damage caused by the storms caused many school districts to close schools until power is restored and debris is cleared.</p><p>Gary's schools have been closed all week. As of Thursday afternoon, <a class="Link" href="https://www.garycsc.k12.in.us/" target="_blank" >Gary Community School Corporation</a> was still waiting for power to return to all of the city's schools. The school district, which is posting <a class="Link" href="https://www.garycsc.k12.in.us/" target="_blank" >regular updates on its website</a>, has not said if schools will reopen next week. </p><p>In a note posted to the <a class="Link" href="https://www.hobart.k12.in.us/" target="_blank" >School City of Hobart’s website</a> Wednesday, superintendent Peggy Buffington said the school district anticipates schools opening on Monday. </p><h3>How have businesses been impacted? </h3><p>Many restaurants, gas stations, grocery stores, banks and small businesses across Northwest Indiana are also still without power. Many businesses remain closed, while others are able to partially operate. </p><p>Gary was Chamber of Commerce President Charles Hughes said he does not have a timeline for when businesses will have power restored because NIPSCO is prioritizing hospitals and homes.</p><h3>What resources are available? </h3><p>Crews from FEMA and the Indiana Department of Homeland Security are assessing the damage across the state. </p><p>Indiana Gov. Mike Braun has also activated <a class="Link" href="https://www.in.gov/dhs/emergency-management-and-preparedness/august-2026-disaster" target="_blank" >the state’s disaster relief fund</a>. Residents can <a class="Link" href="https://app.smartsheet.com/b/form/01a019f5a4457f0495bbef680cff9c75" target="_blank" >apply online for relief funds</a>. Immediate emergency grants are currently capped at $5,000. </p><p>Several community groups are also providing resources and shelter. The YWCA, 150 W. 15th Ave., is offering round-the-clock shelter, warm meals and charging stations. The Monroe Center, 4101 Washington St., is offering emergency shelter to residents whose homes were impacted. Family Life Community Center, 565 Massachusetts St., is distributing hot meals and groceries.</p><p>Capital B Gary has compiled this <a class="Link" href="https://gary.capitalbnews.org/northwest-indiana-storm-relief-resources/" target="_blank" >list of resources</a> for those in need of help, including where to get hot meals, power for their devices and emergency shelter.</p>

entries.title: Which Bears draft picks are pushing for significant roles this season? All of them
entries.summary: <p>CINCINNATI — The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a> will get a good look at their future Saturday. But as their rookies get an extended run against the Bengals, they’re also fighting for immediate roles.</p><p>Six of their seven draft picks are healthy and should play in the preseason game Saturday at Paycor Stadium — only injured linebacker Keyshaun Elliott will miss it — and all of them have a shot at significant jobs for the upcoming season. It’s a little concerning that the Bears are counting on so much from rookies when their roster should be solid by now, but that’s what happens when plans go awry.</p><p>First-round pick <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/04/24/dillon-thieneman-got-to-the-nfl-by-using-criticism-to-improve-thatll-serve-him-well-with-the-bears" >Dillon Thieneman</a> is locked in as a starting safety, and fourth-rounder Malik Muhammad has been auditioning for the starting nickel cornerback spot.</p><p>Tight end Sam Roush, an early third-rounder at No. 69 overall, is basically a first-stringer as coach Ben Johnson leans into using formations with him, Colston Loveland and Cole Kmet together.</p><p>Johnson ran 94 plays with three tight ends on the field last season, fifth in the NFL, and that was when he hadn’t yet acquired the personnel he wanted. He has it with the addition of Roush, and that number could triple this season.</p><p>Wide receiver Zavion Thomas (third round) and defensive tackle Jordan van den Berg (sixth) are pushing the starters at their positions as well.</p><p>Only center Logan Jones, picked in the second round, is earmarked for 2027, though there’s no doubt Johnson will play him this season if at any point he believes him to be an upgrade over veteran Garrett Bradbury.</p><p>All are expected to play against the Bengals, who are sitting their starters. Johnson has not revealed his plans, including whether quarterback Caleb Williams will play. He said last week he didn’t necessarily need to see Williams this preseason, but nothing had been decided concretely.</p><p>With Williams likely to sit or play minimally and backup Tyson Bagent out with a hamstring injury, the Bears will primarily use Case Keenum and undrafted rookie Miller Moss at quarterback.</p><p>Normally, there wouldn’t be so many potential openings for rookies on a team that went 11-6 last season and aspires to be a Super Bowl contender this season. But a combination of underperformance, salary-cap crunches and bad breaks have led the Bears to hang a help wanted sign in the window.</p><p>At safety, the Bears let 2025 starters Kevin Byard and Jaquan Brisker leave in free agency, then spent big on former Seahawks star Coby Bryant. Bryant got hurt a week into training camp and could be out for the season, leaving Thieneman to carry the position.</p><p>They’ve endured similar travails at cornerback, where it looks increasingly likely Muhammad is going snaps outside or at nickel. He’s been at nickel lately as the Bears wait for Kyler Gordon to return and hold their breath to see if he stays healthy.</p><p>With the team unwilling to say whether it expects Gordon back for the Sept. 13 season opener at the Panthers, Muhammad is in line to start that game. If Gordon is good to go for that, there’s a path for Muhammad to start outside if Tyrique Stevenson falters.</p><p>Johnson has pushed for more speed offensively since the Bears hired him, and they drafted wide receiver Luther Burden (4.41 seconds in the 40-yard dash) last year and Thomas (4.28) this year. He absolutely will find ways to turn Thomas loose this season.</p><p>Thomas’ involvement in the offense will depend on how well he grasps the playbook, but the Bears also might need him if Burden’s groin injury drags on longer than projected.</p><p>Van den Berg and undrafted rookie Jayden Loving are knocking on the door at defensive tackle because that position has become somewhat of a free for all.</p><p>Veteran Grady Jarrett wasn’t 100% last season, and durability will continue to be a concern. Gervon Dexter, a 2023 second-round pick, hasn’t impressed the Bears enough to earn a contract extension as he heads into a prove-it season. Jarrett and Dexter will start Week 1, but could see their playing time dip if the rookies are good enough to cut into it.</p><p>On the other side of the line, the Bears are all-in on Bradbury going into the season and have stressed the gap between his ability to lead the offensive line in Year 8 versus Jones’ as a newcomer. Bradbury started in the Super Bowl last season; Jones is about to double his NFL experience Saturday from one preseason game to two.</p><p>It’s not apples to apples because of the added responsibility at center — basically the quarterback of the o-line — but the Bears essentially kept left tackle Ozzy Trapilo on the shelf last season until Week 12, when Johnson believed he was better than Braxton Jones and Theo Benedet.</p><p>It’s precarious to put so much on rookies, but this class has a chance to make the case that it’s ready. They’ve shown a lot of potential in practice the last few weeks, and strong showings in preseason games will weigh heavily with the coaches.</p>

entries.title: Pope Leo watched his namesake White Sox 'Pope Hat' game — and got a hat from the team
entries.summary: <p>Lifelong Chicago White Sox fan Pope Leo XIV tuned into his namesake-themed night where a sold-out crowd wore pontiff-style Sox hats and baseball fans shared a mass "peace be with you" greeting.</p><p>And he was aware the first-place White Sox blew the game in the 10th inning.</p><p>That's according to U.S. Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi, who had an audience with the pope the day after the Aug. 11 5-4 loss to the Cincinnati Reds. </p><p>"He immediately told me that the night before, the White Sox had lost, despite the fact that it was Pope Leo Day at Rate Field," Krishnamoorthi said in an interview with the Chicago Sun-Times Friday. "I was really surprised that he was following the White Sox so religiously, pun intended."</p><p>Krishnamoorthi said the two shared a laugh, and he found it "shocking" that the leader of the Catholic Church was indeed paying attention to his beloved team.</p><p>"He's got this huge entourage, and he's in his beautiful vestments, white vestments. And the first thing he said to me was, 'Can you believe it? The Sox lost last night, and it was Pope Leo Day,'" Krishnamoorthi said. "I was like, 'Oh my gosh.' And my colleagues just burst out in laughter. ... For the pope to bring it up first thing, it's just amazing."</p><p>The White Sox on Friday told the Sun-Times that knowing Pope Leo actually watched his favorite baseball team on "Pope Night" made the night "even better."</p><p>"Thanks to our fans, the ballpark had a wonderful, community feel that night, and hopefully, Pope Leo felt that sense of community through the broadcast," the team said. "We’re only sorry he maybe went to bed — very late — disappointed in the outcome that night."</p><p>The White Sox also sent a gift box to Pope Leo with mementos from the game, including one of the Sox pope hats. </p><p>For his part, Krishnamoorthi brought the pope an unexpected gift: a Chicago Cubs jersey.</p><p>"I thought, well maybe we could give him a Cubs jersey and in the process, hopefully, get some blessings for our beloved Cubs and maybe the chance for an all Chicago World Series someday," Krishnamoorthi said.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" Famed former White Sox organist Nancy Faust returned to her seat to play the national anthem after the first pitch was thrown out by Sister Mary Jo Sobieck of the Dominican Sisters of Springfield. And just before the seventh-inning stretch, the team held a fifth-inning “peace be with you,” led by Evergreen Park and Marist High School alum Rev. Tom Hurley and comedian Pat McGann.</p><p>Former White Sox catcher A.J. Pierzynski also met with Pope Leo at the Vatican in June and presented him with the baseball from the final out of Game 1 of the 2005 World Series, which Pope Leo attended as a fan. Pierzynski recalled his meeting with the pope in a social media post and in interviews and also confirmed the pontiff was paying attention to the Sox.</p><p>"Of course. Of course he is," Pierzynski said in an <a class="Link" href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xB57UgZDk9k&t=36s" target="_blank" >interview with 670 The Score</a> last month. </p><p>Pope Leo has also donned a White Sox hat during a general audience at the Vatican. </p>

entries.title: Encuesta revela que no hay un líder claro en la carrera por la presidencia de la Junta Escolar de Chicago
entries.summary: <p>Un tercio de los votantes probables en las elecciones de noviembre no tiene idea por cuál de los cinco candidatos a la presidencia de la Junta Escolar de Chicago votarían, o incluso si votarán, según una encuesta publicada el jueves que ofrece una de las primeras miradas al estado de la contienda histórica.</p><p>La encuesta a 600 votantes probables, encargada por la campaña del candidato Sendhil Revuluri y realizada la semana pasada, encontró que incluso después de escuchar breves biografías de cada candidato extraídas de materiales de campaña, el 34% de los votantes probables seguía indeciso o dijo que no votaría en la contienda.</p><p><a class="Link" href="https://www.wbez.org/education/2026/05/22/meet-the-candidates-for-chicagos-first-ever-elected-school-board-president" target="_blank" >Ninguno de los cinco aspirantes</a> recibió un respaldo abrumador. La encuesta reveló que el 20% de los votantes probables elegiría a Hilario Domínguez, exdirector político del Sindicato de Maestros de Chicago (CTU), si las elecciones se realizaran hoy. El abogado Victor Henderson quedó en segundo lugar con el apoyo del 14% de los votantes probables.</p><div class="RichTextSidebarModule Enhancement" data-module data-align-center><a class="AnchorLink" id="module-e50000" name="module-e50000"></a> <div class="RichTextModule-items RichTextBody"><h3>La Voz Chicago WhatsApp</h3>Encuentra más noticias en nuestro canal de WhatsApp. <a class="Link" href="https://www.whatsapp.com/channel/0029Vb0XT1XCHDylm3rCs40P" target="_blank" ><b>Síguenos.</b></a></div> </div><p>Los candidatos con experiencia en la junta recibieron el menor respaldo. El exmiembro de la junta, Revuluri, y la miembro actual, Jessica Biggs, obtuvieron cada uno el apoyo del 11% de los votantes probables, mientras que el 9% dijo que votaría por Jennifer Custer.</p><p>Los resultados indican que los candidatos aún tienen trabajo por hacer para diferenciarse y que muchos votantes desconocen una elección a nivel ciudad que tendrá lugar en menos de tres meses. Aunque eso no sorprende porque encuestas anteriores encontraron que <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/education/2025/12/08/few-residents-know-chicago-will-have-a-fully-elected-school-board-poll-finds" target="_blank" >pocos residentes de Chicago</a> sabían que este otoño los votantes elegirán a los 21 miembros de la Junta Escolar de Chicago por primera vez.</p><p>Ethan Axelrod, de la firma de investigación David Binder Research que realizó la encuesta, dijo que más del 80% de los votantes probables no tenía una opinión sobre ninguno de los candidatos antes de escuchar más sobre ellos. Comentó que la encuesta muestra que los residentes de Chicago aún están conociendo a los candidatos y que todavía no prestan atención.</p><p>“Están abiertos a cada uno de estos candidatos, realmente”, destacó Axelrod. “Es una contienda muy fluida”, agregó.</p><p>También es una contienda costosa. Hasta ahora, la mayoría de las donaciones a los candidatos de la junta escolar se han <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/chicago-school-board/2026/07/16/spending-in-chicago-school-board-election-exceeds-1-6-million-as-limits-lift-in-race-for-board-president" target="_blank" >concentrado en la contienda por la presidencia</a>. La encuesta se realizó del 10 al 13 de agosto por teléfono y en línea y tiene un margen de error del 4%.</p><p>Muchos votantes potenciales parecían listos para un cambio. Seis de cada 10 encuestados dijeron que desaprobaban el trabajo que está realizando la junta escolar actual.</p><p>Y cuando se les presentó dos enfoques para abordar <a class="Link" href="https://www.wbez.org/education/2026/05/12/cps-plans-cut-teacher-positions-raise-class-sizes-shrink-723-million-deficit" target="_blank" >el déficit de $732 millones del distrito</a>, algo más de la mitad dijo que sería más probable que votaran por un candidato que pueda “tomar las decisiones difíciles”, mientras que el 36% dijo que elegiría a alguien que “luchará” por más dinero estatal, <a class="Link" href="https://www.wbez.org/education/chicago-school-board/2026/07/30/chicago-school-board-approves-budget-that-reverses-layoffs-but-counts-on-shaky-state-funds" target="_blank" >como la junta actual decidió recientemente en una votación de 11-7</a>.</p><p>En un hallazgo sorprendente, los votantes probables se dividieron casi por igual en torno a los cierres de escuelas.</p><p>Sólo el 46% de los encuestados dijo que sería más probable que votara por alguien que esté “firmemente en contra” de cerrar y consolidar escuelas, mientras que el 42% dijo que sería menos probable que apoyara a un candidato con esa postura.</p><p>El tema ha surgido con frecuencia en los mensajes de campaña dadas las consecuencias de los cierres masivos de escuelas del distrito en 2013. Algunos candidatos se han pronunciado enérgicamente contra cerrar escuelas <a class="Link" href="https://news.wttw.com/2024/09/26/cps-board-votes-unanimously-prohibit-school-closures-until-2027" target="_blank" >cuando se levante una moratoria en todo el distrito</a>, o han intentado presentar a sus oponentes como partidarios de los cierres.</p><p>“El hecho de que esté tan dividido creo que habla del creciente conocimiento de los votantes sobre los problemas presupuestarios que enfrenta el distrito”, recalcó Axelrod.</p><p><i>Traducido con una herramienta de inteligencia artificial (IA) y editado por los seres humanos de </i><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/la-voz" target="_blank" ><i>La Voz Chicago</i></a></p>

entries.title: DJ de Chicago y su esposo son liberados de la custodia de ICE y continúan su batalla legal por asilo
entries.summary: <p>Un DJ local y su esposo han regresado a casa tras ser liberados bajo fianza de la custodia del Servicio de Inmigración y Control de Aduanas (ICE) la semana pasada.</p><p>Omar David Panqueva, conocido como DJ TUNJO, y Santiago Páez <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/la-voz/2026/08/07/inmigracion-detiene-en-el-midway-a-dj-de-suenos-festival-pese-a-tener-un-caso-de-asilo-pendiente" target="_blank" >fueron detenidos el 2 de agosto por agentes federales de inmigración</a> en el Aeropuerto Midway, cuando se disponían a abordar un vuelo a Washington D.C. para comenzar una serie de afterparties de Karol G tras su gira por el país.</p><p>Panqueva actuó en el Sueños Music Festival en Grant Park en mayo y la pareja fundó La Mesa Presents, una organización de música latina y eventos comunitarios con sede en Chicago.</p><div class="RichTextSidebarModule Enhancement" data-module data-align-center><a class="AnchorLink" id="module-040000" name="module-040000"></a> <div class="RichTextModule-items RichTextBody"><h3>La Voz Chicago WhatsApp</h3>Encuentra más noticias en nuestro canal de WhatsApp. <a class="Link" href="https://www.whatsapp.com/channel/0029Vb0XT1XCHDylm3rCs40P" target="_blank" ><b>Síguenos.</b></a></div> </div><p>La pareja, originaria de Colombia, fue liberada bajo fianza el 12 de agosto tras demostrar que no representa riesgo de fuga y que no tiene antecedentes penales, dijo su abogado Enrique Espinoza al Chicago Sun-Times.</p><p>"El gobierno intentó argumentar que representan un riesgo de fuga, pero la realidad es que no lo son. Han cooperado plenamente con el gobierno y han cumplido con todos sus requisitos", dijo Espinoza.</p><p>El Departamento de Seguridad Nacional (DHS) no respondió de inmediato a una solicitud de comentario.</p><p>Panqueva, de 26 años, y Páez, de 27, pidieron asilo tras temer persecución en Colombia por ser parte de la comunidad LGBTQ+. A pesar de su caso de asilo pendiente, DHS dijo que la pareja fue detenida por haber permanecido más tiempo del permitido con visas que obtuvieron en 2021 y que vencieron en 2022.</p><p>Aunque han sido liberados, su batalla legal para permanecer en el país está lejos de terminar, dijo Espinoza. Su detención también les obligó a perder un paso importante en el proceso de asilo.</p><p>Los hombres solicitaron asilo ante el Servicio de Ciudadanía e Inmigración de Estados Unidos (USCIS), que determina si un solicitante cumple los requisitos para recibir asilo. Si esa agencia federal determinara que no califican, su caso normalmente se remitiría a la Corte de Inmigración, donde un juez tomaría la decisión final.</p><p>Pero debido a que fueron detenidos, su caso irá directamente a la corte de inmigración, donde podrían pasar años antes de que tengan la oportunidad de comparecer ante un juez.</p><p>Espinoza dijo que se ha vuelto común detener a personas independientemente de su estatus migratorio con la administración de Trump.</p><p>"El gobierno parece estar deteniendo a cualquiera, independientemente de su historial y de si tiene o no antecedentes penales", comentó Espinoza. "No son los peores de los peores, como lo describen. Son personas que han cumplido con todos los requisitos que exige el gobierno", agregó.</p><p><i>Traducido con una herramienta de inteligencia artificial (IA) y editado por los seres humanos de </i><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/la-voz" target="_blank" ><i>La Voz Chicago</i></a><br></p>

entries.title: Saturday gives Bears coordinator Press Taylor another chance to beat his big brother
entries.summary: <p>CINCINNATI — The game was called “Punt Return.”</p><p>When he was 13, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/halas-intrigue/2026/08/20/bears-bengals-podcast-joint-practice-caleb-williams" target="_blank" >Bengals</a> head coach Zac Taylor would drag his 8-year-old brother Press out onto the 10-yard patch of grass in their Norman, Okla., front yard.</p><p>“I’d throw the ball up,” Zac Taylor said, “and tackle him.”</p><p>At that age, most of their games ended the game way.</p><p>“Me losing and getting upset. …” said Press, who is entering his first year as the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a>’ offensive coordinator. “It wasn’t always fair.”</p><p>As they grew older, the games got more serious — and developed higher stakes. As NFL coaches, they’ve faced each other six times, with outcomes recorded on the Taylor Bro Bowl Trophy, which resides in the office of Sherwood Taylor, their father and former Oklahoma defensive back.</p><p>Saturday’s exhibition game at Paycor Stadium won’t count in the official standings of the NFL — or on the trophy — but Thursday’s joint practice and Saturday’s game provide the perfect excuse for a family reunion. Press’ wife and four kids came to town, as did the coaches’ parents and two sisters.</p><p>When Bears tight end Colston Loveland caught a pass from Caleb Williams and rumbled for a 58-yard touchdown in the final seconds of last year’s road win, Press, who was then the Bears’ pass-game coordinator, took a 3-2-1 lead in the series. When Press worked for the Eagles, they tied the Bengals in 2020.</p><p>“It was the worst,” he said. “We met at midfield and were like, 'What just happened?'”</p><p>The Taylors — Zac is 43 and Press 38 — both played quarterback at the same high school and junior college. Zac transferred to Nebraska and Press to Marshall. They’ve never coached on the same staff, though.</p><p>Zac was plucked off the Sean McVay tree — he was the Rams’ quarterbacks coach — in 2019 and is now the fifth-longest-tenured head coach in the NFL. Press spent seven years with the Eagles and one with the Colts before being named the Jaguars’ offensive coordinator in 2022. He traded off play-calling duties with head coach Doug Pederson for three years before Ben Johnson hired him on his first staff. Johnson promoted him in February to replace Declan Doyle, having been impressed by just how meticulously organized he was.</p><p>Press has film cutups of college and pro games dating back 15 years, sorted by effectiveness against certain schemes and coordinators. Sometimes, during the offseason, he’ll share some of his database with his brother.</p><p>It was that attention to detail that led to the most famous play-call in modern NFL history. When he was a low-level Eagles assistant in 2017, offensive coordinator Frank Reich asked Press for his five best plays. He went into his files and found “Clemson Special,” which the Bears ran against the Vikings the year before. At the 2, quarterback Matt Barkley walked to the line of scrimmage and shifted right. Running back Jeremy Langford took a direct snap left and handed it to Cam Meredith on an end around. Meredith threw to Barkley for a touchdown.</p><p>The Eagles renamed it “Philly Special” and ran it in a Super Bowl win against the Patriots.</p><p>“He's the most organized coach I've ever been around at this level,” said Johnson, who worked with Zac Taylor in Miami. “He's got libraries of plays. He knows when we're going against this defensive coordinator, we can go to this little section that he's already got labeled for that guy and that particular scheme and the things that have given them issues in the past. And that gives us a good starting point each and every week of where we can start with a game plan.”</p><p>The Bears don’t spend a lot of time game-planning for preseason games. Both Taylors, though, want to win.</p><p>“I look forward to getting after him again,” Press said.</p>

entries.title: Mike Mulligan fired as morning host at The Score; Marshall Harris axed as midday host
entries.summary: <p>Mike Mulligan is out at The Score.</p><p>Mulligan, who had been co-host of “Mully and Haugh Show” on The Score (670-AM), reportedly will not return. Also, the station also parted ways with midday co-host Marshall Harris.</p><p>The news was announced by Score vice president Mitch Rosen.<br>“Today, we made some very difficult programming decisions,” said in the memo. “After more than 20 years with The Score, we have parted ways with Mike Mulligan of the ‘Mully and Haugh Show.’”</p><p>Mulligan, who previously was a sportswriter at the Sun-Times, had been with the station for more than 23 years and became a morning co-host in 2008 teaming up with another former Sun-Times sportswriter Brian Hanley on the “Mully and Hanley Show.” Hanley exited the program in 2018 and was replaced by former Tribune sports columnist David Haugh.</p><p>Mully & Haugh won the “Best Morning Show Award” from the Illinois Association of Broadcasters in November of 2025.</p><p>“Mike Mulligan is a Chicago sports media icon,” Haugh posted on X. “A true sports journalist, his versatility had impact, from "The Sports Writers on TV,'' to the Sun-Times, through a tremendous career [at The Score]. He has meant so much to my growth … for which I am forever grateful.”</p>
entries.author: Sun-Times staff

entries.title: Madden '27 Review: Curses? Bears and Caleb Williams better not hope so
entries.summary: <p>The list of players who’ve been touched by “The Curse” is vast.</p><p>“Madden NFL ’99”: Running back Garrison Hearst of the 49ers was the official cover athlete. He broke his fibula in the playoffs a few months later and missed the next two seasons.</p><p>“Madden NFL 2001”: Titans running back Eddie George went from standout to standing around, missing games with injuries and watching his production plummet.</p><p>“Madden NFL 2003”: Rams running back Marshall Faulk saw his streak of 1,000-yard rushing seasons end and dealt with injuries.</p><p>“Madden NFL 2004”: Falcons quarterback Michael Vick, maybe the most unstoppable player in the history of the game franchise, broke his fibula during the 2003 preseason and missed most of the year.</p><p>Donovan McNabb? Injured. Shaun Alexander? Injured. Peyton Hillis? Unproductive and soon out of the league. The most recent victim was 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey, who played just four games in 2024 following the release of “Madden NFL 2025” before bouncing back last season.</p><p>It’s much easier to list those who have avoided the cover curse, such as Patrick Mahomes, Tom Brady and Calvin Johnson.</p><p>So Bears fans might want to start burning some sage, just in case. Thumb your nose at superstition now that quarterback Caleb Williams is on the “Madden NFL 27” cover? You’ve been warned. The other warning that should come with the game is that it’s highly addictive.</p><p>What EA Sports continues to do well is chase authenticity, which benefits football lovers on multiple fronts. EA’s “College Football ’27” feels collegiate. “Madden 27” feels a bit more grown-up and sophisticated, almost like a big brother, as it should.</p><p>There’s a timing-based catching system, which at times feels like pulling off a finishing move in a combat game. There’s a new tackling system based on how aggressive you want the hit to be. But the biggest change and most significant addition to the Franchise Mode is the persona engine. It’s like having the show “Hard Knocks” at your fingertips.</p><p>An NFL locker room is now one big family. In franchise mode, you as the gamer try to keep that family happy — or else see it swallowed up by dysfunction. With more than 65 distinct behaviors, a team captain can go from a foundational piece to a distraction in just a few days of contract negotiations gone bad.Get a deal done and it’s a breaking news alert across the league. Try to save salary-cap space for an aging linebacker who’s popular with the boys? Do so at the risk of a slow-burning mutiny.</p><p>Even better yet is that if you want to just play the games in Franchise Mode and stay away from all the locker room drama, you can hit the “delegate” button and let someone else deal with the behind-the-scenes headaches.</p><p>As usual, the Madden series brings back the pack-ripping Ultimate Team and Superstar modes to chase becoming the G.O.A.T., but it all comes back to improved game play and running the franchise. And that’s where this installment really hits on the details.</p><p>The stadium feel is enhanced. Even the calendar brings the gamer in. During Halloween week, the scoring graphics include cobwebs and pumpkins, just like a real television broadcast would. Weather is more of a factor than it was before, and communication for the visiting team is more of a hassle, as it should be.It feels like football. That’s why “Madden 27” gets a solid B-plus.</p><p>As for “The Curse”? Joining in the spirit of authenticity, I jumped into franchise mode, moved the Bears to Canton, Ohio (Hammond, Indiana, wasn’t available) and upgraded at quarterback by acquiring Super Bowl quarterback Drake Maye (92 rating) for Williams (90 rating) and a mere future draft pick.</p><p>Curse that.</p>
entries.author: Joe Cowley

entries.title: Morgan Maly eager to get her foot in the door with Sky
entries.summary: <p><b>Morgan Maly</b> knew the opportunity might come. She just didn’t tell her parents about it.</p><p>So when the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/chicago-sky" target="_blank" >Sky</a> called to sign her to a development contract, Mom and Dad were shocked initially, then thrilled.</p><p>Maly started packing right away. She’d gotten a sense a couple of weeks earlier that the Sky might be interested, but she didn’t want her parents bugging her about it.</p><p>At the time, the former Creighton standout was at home in Nebraska, preparing to return to her overseas team in Greece.</p><p>Instead, the 24-year-old guard/forward is getting another shot at the WNBA.</p><p>This is Maly’s third crack at the league since graduating from Creighton in 2025. She was cut from the Sun’s training camp roster that year, then spent this preseason with the Mercury.</p><p>Her three-point shooting jumped out to the Sky’s staff. Maly left Creighton as the program’s all-time leader in three-pointers, then shot 36.6% from deep on 6.6 attempts per game last season in Greece.</p><p>“They want me to stretch the floor and provide a perimeter presence from the bigs group,” Maly told the Sun-Times.</p><p>With only seven games remaining, her goals are simple: learn, adapt and be where her feet are. She wants to contribute with her shooting while continuing to develop defensively.</p><p>Overall, though, it’s an opportunity to get her foot in the door.</p><p>Teams retain the rights to their development players, meaning a strong impression over the final few weeks could give Maly another shot at making the Sky roster next spring.</p><p>A few workouts in, Maly is still learning coach <b>Tyler Marsh’s</b> system, but she’s confident about picking it up.</p><p>“It reminds me of college in a way that there’s a primary action that you always get into, and after that you’re making reads based on where the ball goes, what actions work best with the personnel involved,” she said.</p><p>Off the floor, Maly considers herself a foodie and plans to explore the Chicago restaurants she's seen on TikTok.</p><h3><b>Leaving the door open</b></h3><p>At this point, there isn’t much incentive for <b>Skylar Diggins</b> to rush back from a knee injury with the playoffs all but out of reach. But the Sky haven’t officially shut her down for the season.</p><p>Marsh said Diggins has resumed on-court work, including light shooting, and is progressing toward live action.</p><p>If she is intent on returning this season, the upcoming FIBA break gives her additional time. The WNBA pauses from Aug. 31 through Sept. 18.</p><p>Diggins hasn’t played since early July, when she posted on Instagram after being benched and publicly aired frustrations with the organization. </p><p>She has since said she and Marsh have had productive conversations and that her rehab is progressing.</p><h3><b>Foot notes</b></h3><p><b>DiJonai Carrington</b> also did not play against the Valkyries. Carrington missed practice Thursday and Friday because of soreness in her left foot, the same injury that she was rehabbing for most of the season.</p><p>Carrington is averaging 10 points off the bench since returning from injury, though she is shooting a team-worst 34% from the field.</p><p>Marsh is hopeful she will be available Sunday against the Fever. When the teams met earlier this month, Carrington was ejected for a flagrant foul on Fever guard <b>Sophie Cunningham.</b></p>
entries.author: Alissa Hirsh

entries.title: Start of White Sox-Mets game to be delayed by rain
entries.summary: <p>The opening game of this weekend's series between the White Sox and Mets is expected to be delayed by rain, but only by a little bit.</p><p>The White Sox announced shortly after 6pm that the start time of Friday night's game will be pushed back by "approximately" 20 minutes, due to "an approaching wave of rain."</p><p>Even without a tarp on the field at the time of the announcement, the Sox are now planning for a 7pm first pitch. With it being Elvis Night at Rate Field, usually the game is opened by a cadre of people landing in the outfield by parachute to open the festivities, which is still expected to take place at some point.</p><p>Friday night's game also marks the return of former All-Star outfielder Luis Robert Jr. playing his first game back at Rate Field since being traded by the White Sox to the Mets in January, in exchange for utilityman Luisangel Acuña and minor league pitcher Truman Pauley. The scheduled starters for Friday night's tilt are Sean Burke for the White Sox, and Sean Manaea for the Mets.</p>
entries.author: James Fegan

entries.title: Lisle man facing murder charges in fatal drunk driving boat crash on Fox River
entries.summary: <p>A Lisle man is facing murder and a litany of other charges in connection with a fatal drunk boating crash last month on the Fox River, according to the McHenry County State's Attorney’s office.</p><p>Richard Stevenson, 45, is charged with first-degree murder and reckless homicide as well as four counts of aggravated driving under the influence and four counts of operating a Watercraft Under the Influence, according to court records. </p><p>He pleaded not guilty to a number of those charges in court Friday, including felony murder and aggravated driving under the influence as part of a nine-count indictment. </p><p>Magdalena Jablonska, a 48-year-old Des Plaines woman, was on the river with her fiance, Alan Telmini, and their dog July 25 when they were <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2026/07/30/family-mourns-des-plaines-woman-killed-in-boat-crash-over-the-weekend" target="_blank" ><u>hit by a speeding boat</u></a> driven by Stevenson while in a “no wake zone” in suburban McHenry.</p><p>Jablonska was pronounced dead at the scene, according to the McHenry County Coroner’s Office. Telmini was injured and was taken to a nearby hospital. Sasha, the couple's dog, was uninjured.</p><p>Stevenson, whose blood alcohol level was nearly three times the legal limit, was found near the shoreline where his pontoon had come to rest, the McHenry County State's Attorney’s office said. He was arrested and initially charged with one count of reckless homicide and two counts of aggravated DUI causing death.</p><p>Jablonska’s family <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2026/08/06/family-of-marine-veteran-killed-in-fox-river-crash-files-wrongful-death-suit?utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=080726%20Morning%20Edition&utm_content=080726%20Morning%20Edition+CID_b7dd0276464ded8d90a51bd8913fc9f5&utm_source=cst_campaign_monitor&utm_term=Family%20sues%20after%20Fox%20River%20crash&tpcc=cst_cm" target="_blank" ><u>filed a wrongful death lawsuit</u></a> against Stevenson last week.</p><p>The crash is still under investigation by the State Conservation Police with the Illinois Department of Natural Resources. Stevenson is due in court again Sept. 23.</p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2026/07/30/family-mourns-des-plaines-woman-killed-in-boat-crash-over-the-weekend" >Family mourns Des Plaines woman killed in Fox River boat crash over the weekend</a> </li> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2026/08/06/family-of-marine-veteran-killed-in-fox-river-crash-files-wrongful-death-suit" >Family of Marine veteran killed in Fox River crash files wrongful death suit</a> </li> </ul> </div> <p></p>

entries.title: Loyola unveils statue of Sister Jean: 'A tremendous tribute to her life'
entries.summary: <p>When she wasn't courtside on one of Loyola University Chicago's several runs to the NCAA Tournament in the last few years, Sister Jean Dolores Schmidt would watch over the school's students from her office in the Damen Student Center, often keeping her door open so they could visit.</p><p>On Friday, which would have been her 107th birthday, the school honored her legacy by unveiling a statue just southeast of the Joseph J. Gentile Center and the athletic center.</p><p>The sculpture was created by Omaha-artist Littleton Alston to "honor Sister Jean's enduring legacy as an educator and mentor to all Ramblers," reads a plaque next to the statue.</p><p>"It reminds us all that faith, learning, service and sport can unite a community and lift a human spirit," it continues.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> 50 years, described her as "student-centered." Sisler said no matter what role Sister Jean took on, she was always dedicated to pushing students to be better.</p><p>She met Sister Jean as a student at Mundelein College, the Catholic women's college that was later absorbed into Loyola. When Sisler returned as the director of Loyola's Gannon Center for Women and Leadership years later, she almost immediately received a two-page report on priorities she should have the role to best help the students. It was signed off by Sister Jean, of course.</p><p>"She did scouting reports for everybody," Sisler said shortly after the ceremony. "[And] she followed all of her students throughout their professional lives. ... She was very kind but very challenging."</p><p>Sister Jean's nieces Jeannie Tidwell and Janet Schmidt said she had always been an icon to the family, but the last few years had solidified what she meant to the school's community. The former Mundelein students, who also had her as an advisor, reminisced at the ceremony on her love for life's simple pleasures, like basketball and a Potbelly ham sandwich.</p><p>"She was an icon and a role model for me, I always wanted to be like her," Schmidt said. "She always felt a part of the Loyola family anyways. ... She'll never be forgotten."</p><p>The unveiling — which the two joked was Sister Jean's second after her habit came off — also lined up with the first day for the university's incoming freshman class. They said it was one of her favorite times of year as she got to meet the next group of students who would come through the university.</p><p>"It's a tremendous tribute to her life," Tidwell said. "And it's really special that the Loyola community continues to embrace her. ... This is the perfect day for it. entries.title: How we photographed the Illinois State Fair's Governor's Sale of Champions
entries.summary: <p>This week’s top photo comes from Assistant Photo Editor Pat Nabong. Follow her on <a class="Link" href="https://www.instagram.com/patnabong" target="_blank" >Instagram</a>.</p><h3><b>What makes this photo important?</b></h3><p>The Illinois State Fair is a tradition that dates back to 1853. It showcases the state's agricultural and livestock industry while providing visitors with educational experiences, good food and family fun. The Governor's Sale of Champions is one of the highlights of the fair. Prized livestock raised by students involved in 4-H and Future Farmers of America programs were auctioned off. Seventy-one thousand agricultural and livestock farms produce food in Illinois, and 96 percent are owned by families, according to the Illinois Farm Bureau. This photo, which shows the next generation of farmers, is a reflection of that.</p><h3><b>How did you get this photo?</b></h3><p>Families were standing and caring for their livestock while they were waiting for Gov. J.B. Pritzker to arrive for the Governor's Sale of Champions. I was drawn to the bond that the kids had with the animals. I spotted Bowyn Dryer, 4, brushing her family's steer "Big Shooter." I approached while she was brushing the steer, and when she was done, she leaned on the animal and I took a photo.</p><p><b>Technical details:</b><br></p><ul class="rte2-style-ul" entries.title: Allegedly impaired motorist causes wreck that killed motorcyclist on DuSable Lake Shore Drive: police report
entries.summary: <p>An allegedly intoxicated 25-year-old motorist was spotted pouring a bottle of liquid into Lake Michigan after plowing into a motorcycle, killing the woman driving it earlier this week in the Loop, a Chicago traffic crash report said.</p><p>The Chicago woman, who is not being identified because no charges have been filed, was behind the wheel of a Ford Fusion driving south at a high rate of speed in the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2026/08/20/motorcyclist-killed-in-loop-collision-with-car-1-in-custody" target="_blank" >400 block of South DuSable Lake Shore Drive </a>when witnesses saw her rear-end the motorcycle about 11 p.m. Wednesday, knocking the 49-year-old Addison woman off it and leaving her lying in the street, according to the report. </p><p>After the collision, the Ford — with the motorcycle lodged underneath it — burst into flames, jumped the median and ended up facing northbound traffic in the 500 block of South DuSable Lake Shore Drive, according to the report.</p><p>As an off-duty Chicago police officer rushed to render aid to the 49-year-old woman, a witness saw the motorist holding what appeared to be a glass bottle jump out of the car and “run to the lake and pour it into the lake” before returning to her car, according to the report.</p><p></p><p>The still-unidentified Addison motorcyclist was taken to Northwestern Memorial Hospital, where she was pronounced dead at 11:52 p.m. A Friday autopsy determined she died of multiple injuries from the crash and her death was ruled an accident, according to the Cook County medical examiner’s office.</p><p>The driver, who was arrested at the scene, submitted to a breath analysis test, which determined her blood-alcohol was .10, more than .08, which is the legal limit, according to the report.</p><p>The Police Major Accident Investigation Unit is probing the wreck.<br></p>

entries.title: Review: Ricky Martin shows why he’s still the king of Latin pop in Ravinia debut
entries.summary: <p>Ricky Martin had just 30 seconds at this year’s Super Bowl performance to remind the world of his importance in the history of Latin pop music. In 90 minutes at Ravinia Thursday night, he further reclaimed his stake.</p><p>Nothing about his performance in Highland Park was as political as the surprise half-time show appearance in February — when Bad Bunny invited the Puerto Rican megastar to sing “Lo Que Le Paso A Hawaii,” BB’s track decrying gentrification and overtourism of the island state. Still, Martin’s Ravinia debut was a kind of political act.</p><p>After the undue controversy stirred up by an American sporting event’s entertainment wholly in Spanish, Martin soldiered on with a similar commitment during his Ravinia set. Across 20 songs, most of them (including “María,” “Tu Recuerdo” and “Vente Pa’ Ca”) were in his native tongue, performed in an affluent town where 80% of the demographic is white.</p><div While there weren’t detailed buildouts of a casita or a sugar cane field like at the Super Bowl, Ravinia did have salsa lessons and open dancing, led by West Loop’s Latin Rhythms.</p><p>“We’re going to teach you some moves so when Ricky comes out, we’re ready to go,” said the instructor.</p><p>There was an opening set of traditional music at the Carousel Stage from the Latin Music Project, organized by the Puerto Rican Arts Alliance. Casa Famosa had a tent selling its hard agua frescas. There was even a jumbotron set up on the north side of the lawn so patrons could see all of Martin’s incredible dance moves and follow along. And fans did so, waving Puerto Rican flags, proudly wearing blue-white-and-red paraphernalia and donning traditional pava straw hats.</p><p>If there was ever any doubt of the importance of the Latin music explosion that has reached a new fever pitch, one only needed to look around the park at Ravinia for verification. According to a Ravinia spokesperson, it was one of the venue’s biggest shows of the summer so far.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="line"></span><div class="Figure-credit"><p>Victor Hilitski/For the Sun-Times</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p>We have Ricky Martin to thank for much of the genre’s ascent.</p><p>More than 40 years ago, his appearance as a pre-teen in the Puerto Rican boy band Menudo set off a chain reaction that led to one of the most successful breakout careers for a solo pop artist on a global stage. Since hailed the “King of Latin Pop,” Martin is widely credited for the gate busting that helped usher in the Shakira, J Lo and Karol G kingdom. Bad Bunny paid back Martin with the Super Bowl cameo.</p><p>Thursday’s Ravinia set felt just as momentous. The lawn and the stage inside the Hunter Pavilion were busting at the seams with pop spectacle. “I just had a couple of days at home. I’m coming full of energy. I’m ready for a party tonight!” Martin declared — and he delivered.</p><p>The show was his first performance in the States, months after a run of appearances in Europe and Asia, and Martin pounced on the opportunity to show what he was still remarkably made of at 54.</p><p>But it wasn’t just his well-preserved dance moves and vocal tenor, or the never-ending parade of ab-bearing frocks and sweat towels he teased all night. It was also the excellent eight-piece band (with full horn section) and dozen-member dance squad that brought pure electricity to the night and demonstrated why Latin music is always so alive and communal.</p><p>The audience got to its feet when Martin launched into the tropicalia mix of “Pégate.” Even through the heartfelt ballads, such as his personal favorite Franco de Vita’s “Vuelve,” a dropped bomb couldn’t have turned eyes away from him. Of course, perennial hits “She Bangs,” “Livin’ La Vida Loca” and “Nobody Wants to Be Lonely” (with a video from the song’s collaborator Christina Aguilera) ignited the mixed crowd.</p><p>The renewed reaction to his music over the past year seems to have only reignited Martin, too. Before the show was over — with a balloon-dropping finale of his World Cup anthem “The Cup of Life” — Martin teased a return “very soon” with new music and poked fun at his own longevity.</p><p>“I think I’m gonna be 85 years old and still be performing because I just love it,” he said, referencing the Rolling Stones. “As long as you allow me to, I’ll be here.”</p><h3>Ravinia 2026 set list </h3><p>Pégate<br>María<br>Adrenalina (Wisin song)<br>Love You For A Day<br>Bombón De Azúcar<br>Vuelve (Franco De Vita song)<br>Shake Your Bon-Bon<br>Que Rico<br>Lola, Lola<br>La Bomba<br>She Bangs<br>Private Emotion (The Hooters cover)<br>Nobody Wants To Be Lonely<br>Te Extrano<br>Tu Recuerdo<br>La Mordidita<br>Por Arriba, Por Abajo<br>Vente Pa' Ca<br>Livin' La Vida Loca<br>The Cup Of Life </p>
